body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The fair has packed up and the week is underway, but the heat is staying put — we're looking at a high near 101 today with moderate air quality and no active weather alerts. The top story this morning is a big change on the local gym scene: Body Xchange has been acquired by Planet Fitness, and its Bakersfield locations are closing. Also overnight, a pursuit south of town ended in a foot chase and a K9 search near Cottonwood Road and White Lane.

## The Kern Overnight

A vehicle that failed to stop drew a pursuit shortly before 11 p.m. that ran south on Wible Road past Panama Lane at speeds around 40 mph. Traffic was light, and officers held off on any pursuit-intervention attempt as the driver headed toward a dead end. The chase turned into a foot pursuit, with air support overhead and a K9 track leading into a rural property of shacks and horse pens between Cottonwood Road and White Lane. A subject was seen going into a mobile home on East Panama Lane, and the K9 made contact with a person at the front gate behind a parked truck as officers swept the property through the midnight hour.

Elsewhere, crews were sent at 12:31 a.m. to a single-story commercial building in the 1300 block of Kern Street for smoke in the bathroom ventilation of a mechanics warehouse. Engine 21 found light smoke showing and took command of a minor incident, with workers already on scene. At 2:06 a.m., crews responded to a recycling facility in the 2600 block of South Mount Vernon Avenue for a reported brush fire and found a large fire in the compost area, roughly 10 by 20 feet. They called the facility to bring in tractors and employees, dumped the water they had, and Engine 41 stayed until staff arrived to take over.

Just before 10 p.m., someone tried to strong-arm a person outside a fast-food restaurant in the 2400 block of North Chester Avenue. The suspect, in a blue shirt and blue jeans, fled on foot. At 10:42 p.m., a semi-truck with a black bed full of hay was taken from the 900 block of South MLK Boulevard; the reporting party tracked it heading south on Cottonwood Road near White Lane. Traffic units also spent the evening on a four-vehicle crash on Mount Vernon Avenue, a pedestrian struck in a three-vehicle crash on Riverlakes, and a hit-and-run at South P Street and Bell Terrace. The rest of the log was alarms, medical aids and disturbances.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 101 degrees and a low around 71 tonight. It's currently 77 at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality sits at 66 — moderate, so most folks can go about their day, though sensitive groups may want to take it a little easier during the hottest hours. No active fires are being reported. If you're working outside today, the usual advice holds: water early, shade when you can, and keep an eye on neighbors who live alone.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Body Xchange has been acquired by Planet Fitness, and the gym chain's Bakersfield locations are closing.** The change means members who have been working out at Body Xchange clubs around town will need to find a new place to train, and it marks the departure of a local fitness brand in favor of a national one. If you hold a membership, it's worth checking on the status of your plan and what happens to any prepaid time.

**According to 23ABC, Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders drew a large crowd Sunday night inside Harvey Auditorium at Bakersfield High School as part of a three-day tour through California.** The stop was in support of Randy Villegas, the Democratic challenger running against Republican Congressman David Valadao in California's 22nd Congressional District. Sanders called on voters to back progressive candidates, and healthcare dominated the night — both men criticized Valadao over his 2025 vote for President Trump's "Big Beautiful Bill," which is projected to cut federal spending on Medicaid and other health programs by more than $1 trillion over a decade. Sanders pointed to the district's high share of Medicaid recipients, while Valadao has previously said his vote preserves the program for its intended recipients — children, pregnant women, the disabled and the elderly — and reflects the district's priorities.

**KGET 17 also reports that the Supreme Court is set to hear a case Monday on whether localities can sue oil companies for climate damages.** The outcome matters well beyond the courtroom, and it matters here in particular: Kern County is one of the state's largest oil-producing regions, so any ruling on how far cities and counties can reach in climate litigation could ripple through local budgets, industry operations and the legal landscape that surrounds them.

**23ABC tells us that a 14-year-old girl was injured Thursday when her electric scooter collided with a vehicle in Arvin, near the CVS on Bear Mountain Boulevard.** Police say her injuries were minor and not life-threatening, but the crash lands alongside new national data showing e-scooter injuries among children are surging — an analysis of federal injury data by E-Ride Hero estimates nearly 29,000 kids aged 14 and younger were hurt in 2025, up 64% from 2024 and nearly 700% since 2020. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Joshua Deutinger said officers are seeing more e-scooter crashes as the devices grow in popularity, and he reminded riders that they still have to follow the rules of the road, stay in bike lanes, and hold a valid driver's license to operate on the street. Kids, he said, shouldn't be riding them on roadways posted above 25 mph at all.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a man has been convicted in the deadly stabbing of the mother of his children here in Bakersfield.** The conviction closes a chapter in a case that has weighed on the families involved and on the neighborhoods around it, and it now moves toward sentencing.

## Something good

The Kern County Fair wrapped up Sunday, and the heat didn't keep families away. Erin Sceales told 23ABC she was excited to be back after four or five years away — "It's the hottest day, of course. But we're excited" — and she loved that the fair lets her older kids split off with friends while she and the little ones hit the kiddie rides. Phelicia Palmer came on the final day with her grandchildren, the baby enjoying his first fair and his sister her second. "You're never too old," she said. That's a good note to end the season on.

## Coming up this week

It's a full week of public meetings, so if you've got something on your mind, there's a room for it. The Youth Commission meets today, Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. Tuesday brings the Police Civil Service Commission at 8:30 a.m. Wednesday is the busy one: City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m., followed by City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. On Thursday, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon, and Friday the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee gathers at noon as well. Looking a little further out, the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets Monday, October 12, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a run of shows lined up. Tonight, Monday, October 5, it's Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein. Friday, October 9, brings the NB RIDAZ: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. United We Dance: Festival Energy takes the stage Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour comes through Saturday, October 17. If you're already thinking ahead to next season, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 is also on sale.

Have a good Monday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there.

top.title: Body Xchange acquired by Planet Fitness, locations in Bakersfield close
